style: factual clickbait for China finance audience

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一

briefs.current_title: 巴克莱辛格：AI交易逻辑生变，亚洲科技谁主沉浮？

subtitles.zh: 当然，谢谢邀请我参加节目。
subtitles.en: Yeah, absolutely, I'm wanting even, and thanks for having me on.

subtitles.zh: 市场基本上在告诉我们，已经从交易AI氛围和叙事，转向对盈利超预期设定更高门槛。
subtitles.en: Look, I think markets are basically telling us that we are going on from, moving on from trading AI vibes and narrative, to now requiring a pretty high bar for what an earnings beat looks like.

subtitles.zh: 这既体现在资本开支的前瞻指引上，也体现在变现路径上。
subtitles.en: And you know, that's both in terms of capex forward guidance, but also for the path of monetization.

subtitles.zh: 隔夜看Meta和特斯拉，有两点很突出，
subtitles.en: And when I look at meta and Tesla overnight, the two things that stand out to me is,

subtitles.zh: 特斯拉的价格走势说得通，因为公司确实指引明年资本开支下降。
subtitles.en: you know, Tesla's price action kind of makes sense because the company did guide for lower capex next year.

subtitles.zh: 但Meta的数据客观上很强，然而亚洲今早开盘后，其股价却难以守住涨幅。
subtitles.en: But meta's numbers were objectively strong and yet the stock struggled to hold on to its gains when Asia came in this morning.

subtitles.zh: 这对亚洲后续走势的启示是，我们有三个科技表达指数，
subtitles.en: So what that tells me for the path ahead for Asia, where we have three indices, you know, for tech expression,

subtitles.zh: 韩国、台湾和日本，明年市场将更加挑剔。
subtitles.en: Korea, Taiwan and Japan, is that the market is going to be a lot more discerning next year.

subtitles.zh: 我认为要尊重价格走势，我们考虑做多优质资产。
subtitles.en: And I think respecting price action there, we think about being long quality.

subtitles.zh: 尤其是在科技领域，进入明年之际。
subtitles.en: Especially in the tech space, heading into next year.

briefs.speaker: Kanhari Singh
briefs.speaker_context: Barclays, Head of Asia Equity Derivatives Sales (joining from Barclays Asia Forum in Singapore)
briefs.current_title: 巴克莱辛格：中国政策信号转向，财政刺激为何不急？

subtitles.zh: 这是个好问题。思考中国大局，甚至回溯到重启交易，市场明显在寻找财政刺激的大标题。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, that's a pretty good question. I think when I think about the big picture in China, and even if I go as far back as the reopening trade, the market has clearly looked for some large headlines around fiscal stimulus.

subtitles.zh: 2024年9月我们确实看到了直接权益市场刺激。对我们来说，这在中国很多方面是一种实验，试图通过强力广泛支持权益市场，从消费者角度激发正向财富效应。
subtitles.en: And we did get that in terms of direct equity markets stimulus in September 2024. And you know, to us in many ways, that was China's way of kind of experimenting with trying to see if positive wealth effects can be kicked in on a consumer f

subtitles.zh: 但思考2025年，我们基本上已从中国权益市场中排除财政刺激的右尾风险。
subtitles.en: But when I think about 2025, we moved on to essentially price that right tail out from Chinese equity markets on fiscal stimulus.

subtitles.zh: 我认为有合理原因。看今年经济，中国增长呈非常K型路径，低于预期，但出口等领域受半导体驱动异常强劲。
subtitles.en: And I think for the right reasons, you know, when we look at the economy this year, it's been a very k-shaped path for China growth is below expectations, but pockets of the economy like exports are doing exceptionally strong driven by semi

subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，出口复苏在一定程度上与汇率强势脱钩，这说明中国在出口价值链上也在上移。
subtitles.en: What's been interesting is that that export recovery is somewhat decoupling from the effect strength as well, which tells you that China is moving up in the value chain of exports as well.

subtitles.zh: 所以从政策角度看，并不急于推出大规模财政刺激，权益市场支持仍非常有针对性以扭转局面。
subtitles.en: So I think from a policy perspective, there is no rush here to come in to do big fiscal stimulus and equity market support is still extremely targeted to turn things around.

briefs.speaker: Kanhari Singh
briefs.speaker_context: Barclays, Head of Asia Equity Derivatives Sales (joining from Barclays Asia Forum in Singapore)
briefs.current_title: 巴克莱辛格：印尼市场评级下调，被动资金流出压力几何？
current_title_lines: 被动资金流出压力几何？

subtitles.zh: 当然。我认为现在宣布确实令人意外，尽管之前明显有铺垫。
subtitles.en: Yeah, absolutely. Look, I think it's definitely been, you know, a surprise in terms of the announcement coming now, even though there was clearly a build up to it.

subtitles.zh: 印尼资产在这些水平相当便宜。权益资产显然有大波动，MSCI印尼前瞻估值现在是全球流动性变化以来最便宜。
subtitles.en: Indonesian assets are pretty cheap at these levels. Equities have obviously had some very large moves, MSCI Indonesia on a forward valuation basis is now as cheap as it's been since GFC.

subtitles.zh: 印尼盾实际汇率是20多年来最便宜。
subtitles.en: And the Indonesian rupee in real terms is the cheapest that it's been in over 20 years.

subtitles.zh: 所以显然印尼资产便宜，但我认为2027年6月前可能更便宜，除非治理方面有非常强的缓解因素。
subtitles.en: So clearly Indonesian assets are cheap, but I think there's a possibility that they get even cheaper in June, 20, 27 unless there are some very strong mitigating factors from a governance perspective.

subtitles.zh: 我们预计约150亿美元被动权益资金流出，认为美元印尼盾可能在明年二季度前升至1850水平。
subtitles.en: We're expecting about 15 billion US dollars in passive equity outflows and we think dollar idea is likely to grind higher to 18 to 50 level by a second quarter of next year.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这对权益资产意味着，除非MSCI希望看到的情况出现非常强的转变。
subtitles.en: And I think what that means for equities is, you know, unless again, there is a very strong turnaround in terms of what MSCI wants to see.

subtitles.zh: 权益资产反弹可能被卖出，进入明年。
subtitles.en: Equity rallies are probably going to be sold and you know, I'm heading into next year.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这仍是非常局部的国内故事，公告发布时印尼在新兴市场指数中权重为50个基点。
subtitles.en: I think this is a very localized domestic story still when this announcement came out Indonesia's weight in EM indices was 50 bips.

subtitles.zh: 所以这绝不是更广泛的新兴亚洲传染故事，尽管印尼本地波动剧烈。
subtitles.en: So by no means is this is this a broader even EM Asia contagion story, I would say as violent as the moves have been locally in Indonesia.

briefs.speaker: Marc Raibert
briefs.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute
briefs.current_title: 波士顿动力创始人：人形机器人竞赛，中国领先还是美国领先？
current_title_lines: 中国领先还是美国领先？

subtitles.zh: 您对这样的发展速度印象深刻吗？中国是否可能在人形机器人领域继续领先并扩大对美国的优势？
subtitles.en: Have you been impressed by the pace and could, you know, China continue to lead and extend its lead over the US perhaps when it comes to humanite robots.

subtitles.zh: 我不从竞争的角度思考，也不确定是否同意中国领先或不领先。但我确实认为现在是机器人领域的绝佳时机，关注度极高，资源丰富，投资者众多，大量事情正在发生。
subtitles.en: So, you know, I don't think in terms of a competition and I'm not sure I agree that China is leading or not leading. I do agree that it's a fantastic time to be in robotics. There's so much attention. There's so much resources, investors, a

subtitles.zh: 你说得对。过去几年，强化学习这项技术席卷全球。多个团队开创了这项工作，现在企业可以将这些技术应用到自己的机器人上。
subtitles.en: You're right. Over the last couple of years, reinforcement learning is a technique that's really swept the globe. A number of different groups originated the work and now it's made it possible for a company to take their robot, apply those

subtitles.zh: 几乎立刻就能让机器人做出令人兴奋的新动作，就像在中国奥运会上看到的那样，或其他公司运用这些技术所做的展示。
subtitles.en: And almost immediately get it to do new, exciting things like you see at the Chinese Olympics or you see other companies using those techniques to do.

subtitles.zh: 我们看到机器人举汽车、后空翻，但真正让机器人做人类动作一直很热门。我的同事大卫说，我们希望看到机器人拖地，但人类看似基本的动作并不容易做到。
subtitles.en: You know, we see those robots lifting cars and doing backflips, but it's been hot for robots to actually do human action. I mean, David, my colleague was talking about we would love to see a robot mopping the floor, but it's not that easy t

subtitles.zh: 完全正确。我认为部分问题在于人们不了解人类在自己所做的事情上有多出色。
subtitles.en: Absolutely true. I think part of the problem is that people don't understand how good human beings are at what they do.

subtitles.zh: 人类拥有多才多艺、灵巧以及其他特征。我认为根本问题在于，把这些机器人称为人形机器人本身就有问题。
subtitles.en: And what versatility and dexterity and other features that humans have. I mean, I think at the root of it, there's a problem even in calling these robots humanoid.

subtitles.zh: 因为人形意味着什么？是两条手臂、两条腿和一个头吗？为什么可能有上百家公司在制造有两条手臂、两条腿和一个头的机器人？
subtitles.en: Because what does humanoid mean? Does it mean two arms, two legs and a head? Why are there maybe a hundred companies building robots with two arms, two legs and a head?

subtitles.zh: 真正的人形应该意味着情境意识、理解周围环境、移动能力、灵巧性，以及用手或身体其他部位以有用方式移动物体的能力。
subtitles.en: When really humanoid should mean situational awareness, understanding our surroundings, mobility, dexterity, ability to use our hands or other parts of our body to move things around in a useful way.

subtitles.zh: 语义理解，更深入地理解世界。所有这些要素让人类擅长所做之事，也让某些动物擅长它们所做之事。
subtitles.en: Semantic understanding, understanding the world in a deeper way. All those ingredients are what make humans good at what they do and some animals good at what they do.

You are a Chinese viral-title angle architect. Return strict JSON only. Do not write a safe summary. Generate competing, fact-grounded emotional angles for each clip. Operating rule: 二极管法则
- A candidate is usable only if one emotion pole is unmistakable and emotion_tension is at least 8/10.
- The six permitted poles are: unexpected reversal, pleasant surprise, strong doubt, finally-someone-said-it candor, verified words-versus-actions contrast, and fact-based pride in a Chinese comparative advantage.
- Do not split the emotion across several mild ideas. Pick one pole and push it to the factual limit.
- A question mark is not emotion. "前景如何", "回报路径在哪", "能否实现", "面临哪些挑战", "回报存疑", and "释放什么信号" score at most 4 unless they contain a concrete contradiction or consequence.

Angle rules:
- surprise_reversal: state the familiar baseline, then expose the source claim that reverses it. Do not turn a baseline contrast into "改口" unless research.position_change.supported is true with at least two independent sources.
- outsider_candor: use only when a foreign institution/expert says something unusually direct. Keep the identity contrast in evidence_basis and viewer_reaction, then realize it in final copy by placing the specific surprising claim against its consequence. Never literally output 外资策略师、外资首席、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话, or 西方机构承认.
- words_vs_actions: use only when research.words_vs_actions.supported is true and independent_source_count is at least 2. Show the two exact sides in question form. Never directly call anyone a liar.
- china_advantage: use only when research.china_advantage.supported is true. Put the concrete Chinese advantage or the foreign competitor's forced response in the foreground. The emotional direction must favor China.
- authority_breaks_consensus: the authority must be recognizable to a China audience, or be labeled by a meaningful role. Do not lead with an obscure romanized name.
- concrete_stakes: expose a specific number, forced choice, consequence, or who gains/loses. Generic importance is not a stake.

Writing rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Produce exactly four candidates per clip and use at least three different angle_id values when the evidence permits.
- Each candidate has exactly three short title lines. Think cover blocks, not a newspaper sentence.
- Ideal line lengths are 3-10, 4-12, and 5-14 Chinese characters. Full title is ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- The title must reveal enough familiar context to create a small information gap, then withhold the explanation supplied by the video.
- Prefer concrete verbs and consequences: 逼急、藏不住、说透、砍半. Use only when facts support them. "改口" requires research.position_change.supported with two independent sources; words-versus-actions phrases require research.words_vs_actions.supported with two independent sources.
- Do not mechanically copy examples or proper nouns from instructions. Derive every noun, number, actor, and comparison from this clip and its evidence card.
- angle_id, emotion_pole, and viewer_reaction are private editorial metadata. Never copy their wording into title or title_lines.
- Final cover structure should be [specific subject] / [unexpected fact or comparison] / [concrete unresolved consequence], not [speaker category] / [editorial label] / [topic].
- If a person or institution is genuinely recognizable, use its verified proper name. If it is not recognizable, omit the identity and lead with the subject and fact; do not replace it with generic labels such as 外资策略师 or 海外专家.
- For names and technical terms, use only the current clip's verified title_label. Never use official_zh/legal company names as cover copy, and never invent a Chinese transliteration when title_label is empty or English.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is a source label, not the expert or actor. Company legal suffixes do not belong in a title.
- For China-related clips, never attack China or imply national decline. Favor confidence, competence, policy room, industrial strength, cost advantage, talent, resilience, and competitors being forced to respond.
- If the clip is negative about China and no constructive factual angle exists, use a neutral mechanism question instead of nationalist or doom framing.
- Forbidden title words: 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.
- Forbidden hard-negative wording: 经济危机、金融危机、债务危机、危机、崩盘、崩溃、完了、没救、惨了.
- Do not use sensitive geopolitical or military subjects, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbered prefixes.
- If evidence cannot support four dramatic factual claims, vary the framing and use strong questions; never fabricate the missing drama.

4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.

- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.
- Do not use flat endings such as 回报路径在哪、回报存疑、前景如何、未来如何、有待观察、仍不明朗、面临挑战、带来机遇、释放信号、关键分叉在哪、有望扩大. Turn the caveat into a concrete unresolved action or contradiction.
- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.
- Title fields must not contain 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.

briefs.speaker: Marc Raibert
briefs.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute
briefs.current_title: 波士顿动力创始人：人形机器人五年后能做什么？仓库工厂先行，家庭尚远
current_title_lines: 仓库工厂先行，家庭尚远

subtitles.zh: 我认为如果我们专注于这一点，并涉及多种形态——形态意味着两条腿、两条手臂和一个头，或者轮子和另一种身体，或者六条手臂——那么像人类一样多才多艺和有用的可能性真的没有极限。
subtitles.en: And I think if we focused on that, with a variety of morphologies involved, morphologies means two legs, two arms and a head or wheels and some other kind of body or maybe six arms, there's really no limit to what could be versatile and use

subtitles.zh: 话虽如此，马克，我想知道哪些是炒作，哪些不是。五年后，这些你喜不喜欢这个称呼都罢的人形机器人，能做什么？
subtitles.en: So having said that, Mark, I'm wondering what's hype, what's not, five years down the road, what might these humanoid robots, whether you like the term or not, what would they be able to do?

subtitles.zh: 很难预测。容易说的是，各种形状和形式的机器人已经在仓库等场所使用，那些地方非常有序，物体处理量很大。
subtitles.en: It's hard to predict. I think that the easy thing to say is robots of various shapes and forms are already being used in warehouses and places like that, very organized things where there's objects being handled at very high volume.

subtitles.zh: 在难以获得人力劳动的地方，人力流动率高，人口老龄化，人口减少，年轻人对某些工作的态度在改变，一些群体的熟练劳动力正在老化退出。
subtitles.en: And where it's hard to get human labor, human labor has a lot of turnover, there's aging populations, reduced populations, a lot of the attitudes towards some kinds of work is changing among young people, some populations are aging out for

subtitles.zh: 所以机器人能做什么这个谜题有很多拼图。
subtitles.en: So there's a lot of pieces to the puzzle of what robots are going to be able to do.

subtitles.zh: 总之，我开始说，我认为仓库之后，工厂可能是下一个，家庭则要远一些，因为家庭需要大量安全保障，需要极致安全，需要低成本让消费者买得起，还需要它们能在家里做有用的事。
subtitles.en: Anyway, I start to say, I think warehouses are now factories are probably next, I think our homes are going to be a little ways out because for homes you need a lot of safety, you need really ultimate safety, you need low cost for consumers

subtitles.zh: 考虑到每个人的房子不同，杂物不同，孩子在场且脆弱，这确实是真正的挑战。
subtitles.en: And given that everybody's house is different, everybody's junk is different, everybody's kids are there and vulnerable, it's a real challenge.

briefs.speaker: Marc Raibert
briefs.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute
briefs.current_title: 波士顿动力创始人：机器人威胁论被夸大？机会远大于风险
current_title_lines: 被夸大？机会远大于风险

subtitles.zh: 人们对与机器人共处以及机器人的潜力有很多焦虑。
subtitles.en: There's a lot of anxiety among people when it comes to being amongst robots and the potential of robots.

subtitles.zh: 你这么说，但我演讲时带这些机器人去展会，人们也很喜欢看。
subtitles.en: You say that, but I take these robots around to shows when I give talks and people love to see here too.

subtitles.zh: 是的，现在外面就有一个，人们喜欢看它们，喜欢和它们合影。
subtitles.en: Yeah, there's one right out there now and people love to see them, they love to pose with them.

subtitles.zh: 直到它们成为威胁，或直到它们接管工作，直到我们谈论可能的人类灭绝。
subtitles.en: Until they become a threat or until they take over the jobs until, until we talk about possibly the extinction of humankind.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这些都是抽象概念，并不像人们想的那么迫在眉睫。
subtitles.en: I think those are all abstract ideas that aren't as present as people think.

subtitles.zh: 我认为媒体更喜欢谈论这些，好莱坞当然靠你刚提到的三件事蓬勃发展，我希望我能记住具体是什么。
subtitles.en: I think the media likes to talk about those things more and certainly Hollywood thrives on those three things you just mentioned, I wish I could remember exactly what they were.

subtitles.zh: 那些威胁，我认为机会……看，我们应该认真对待风险，努力提供机器人安全保障，提供监管和控制。
subtitles.en: You know, the threat, all those threats, I think the opportunities, look, we should take the risks seriously and work on providing safety in the robots, providing regulation and control.

subtitles.zh: 但我们不应以限制所有机会的方式来做，因为机会巨大，我希望我们能利用这些机会。
subtitles.en: But we shouldn't do it in a way that limits all the opportunities because the opportunities are vast and I'm hoping we get to take advantage of that.

subtitles.zh: 越来越多的人说我们需要放缓AI发展，你在这场辩论中持什么立场？
subtitles.en: There is a growing chorus of people who say, we need to slow down the development of AI, where do you sit on that debate?

subtitles.zh: 我不参与那场辩论，我不知道，我觉得这有些过度紧张，但我们拭目以待。
subtitles.en: I'm not sitting on that debate, I don't know, it seems overwrought to me, but you know, we'll see.

subtitles.zh: 最坏的情况是什么？
subtitles.en: What's the worst case scenario?

subtitles.zh: 我参加过一个政府监管机构的国际会议，有些人只谈论可能发生的最坏情况。
subtitles.en: You know, I went to a meeting, an international meeting of government regulators and some of them would only talk about the worst possible thing that could happen.

subtitles.zh: 我认为那不是正确的立场，我们需要谈论机会与风险的平衡。
subtitles.en: I don't think that's the right place to be, again, we need to talk about the balance of opportunity versus risks.

subtitles.zh: 如果只关注最坏情况，我们都会把自己锁在家里，因为可能有车经过而受伤。
subtitles.en: And if you just focus on the worst possible thing, I mean, we'd all be locked in our houses because a car might go by and we get hurt.

briefs.speaker: Marc Raibert
briefs.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute
briefs.current_title: 波士顿动力创始人：机器人未来最兴奋的是什么？生产力机会巨大
current_title_lines: 最兴奋的是什么？生产力机会巨大

subtitles.zh: 让我们谈谈最积极的事情。
subtitles.en: So let's talk about the most positive thing.

subtitles.zh: 在机器人领域，你最兴奋的是什么？
subtitles.en: I mean, what are you most excited about when it comes to robotics?

subtitles.zh: 我们今天在哪里？
subtitles.en: Where are we today?

subtitles.zh: 我们将走向何方？
subtitles.en: Where are we headed?

subtitles.zh: 有没有可能发生难以想象的事情？
subtitles.en: I mean, anything that is possibly the unimaginable that could happen?

subtitles.zh: 我试着给出两种答案。
subtitles.en: I'll try and give two kinds of answers.

subtitles.zh: 我是研究员和开发者，对我来说不全是赚钱，而是取得技术进步和创造新事物。
subtitles.en: So I'm a researcher developer and it's not all about making money for me, it's about making the technical advances and creating new things.

subtitles.zh: 而且不一定看得到终点。
subtitles.en: And you know, there's no necessarily end point in sight.

subtitles.zh: 看看计算机。
subtitles.en: I mean, look at computers.

subtitles.zh: 他们造出又大又单一速度运行的计算机，然后它们变得更小更快。
subtitles.en: You know, they made computers that were big and operated at one speed and then they got smaller and faster.

subtitles.zh: 现在你可以随身携带，技术发展没有极限。
subtitles.en: Now that you can carry them around, there's no limit to where the technology goes.

subtitles.zh: 机器人也是如此。
subtitles.en: And robots are like that, too.

subtitles.zh: 现在很多人专注于制造有两条手臂、两条腿和一个头的东西，但也许我们会有些奇怪的新东西。
subtitles.en: You know, right now a lot of people are focused on trying to make things with two arms, two legs and a head, but you know, maybe we'll have some weird new thing that we're going to.

subtitles.zh: 这是我作为研究员的一面。
subtitles.en: So that's the researcher side of me.

subtitles.zh: 我确实认为每个人的生产力都有限制。
subtitles.en: I do think that there's limitations to productivity for everybody.

subtitles.zh: 正如我之前所说，人口老龄化，人口减少，人们不像以前那么愿意从事某些行业。
subtitles.en: I think the, as I said before, there's aging population, there's declining populations, there's people who don't really want to work in the trades as much as they did.

subtitles.zh: 别误会，机器人还做不到水管工或电工的工作，但我认为它们将来可以。
subtitles.en: Now don't get me wrong, robots aren't up to doing what a plumber or electrician does yet, but they will be, I think.

subtitles.zh: 所以有机会在不一定有足够人力做所有这些事的情况下实现高生产力。
subtitles.en: So there's an opportunity to have high productivity without necessarily having people available to do all those things.

briefs.speaker: John Sawers
briefs.speaker_context: Former Chief of MI6 (UK Secret Intelligence Service)
briefs.current_title: 英前情报首长：日本想建CIA？情报自主成新趋势

subtitles.zh: 这是一个碎片化的世界，越来越多的国家想要更多情报。日本就是例子。
subtitles.en: It is a fragmented world and more and more countries are wanting more intelligence. Case in point, Japan.

subtitles.zh: 它想组建类似CIA的机构。你怎么看？
subtitles.en: It wants to form what is similar to the CIA. What do you make of that?

- A candidate is usable only if one emotion pole is unmistakable and emotion_tension is at least 8/10.
- The six permitted poles are: unexpected reversal, pleasant surprise, strong doubt, finally-someone-said-it candor, verified words-versus-actions contrast, and fact-based pride in a Chinese comparative advantage.
- Do not split the emotion across several mild ideas. Pick one pole and push it to the factual limit.
- A question mark is not emotion. "前景如何", "回报路径在哪", "能否实现", "面临哪些挑战", "回报存疑", and "释放什么信号" score at most 4 unless they contain a concrete contradiction or consequence.

Angle rules:
- surprise_reversal: state the familiar baseline, then expose the source claim that reverses it. Do not turn a baseline contrast into "改口" unless research.position_change.supported is true with at least two independent sources.
- outsider_candor: use only when a foreign institution/expert says something unusually direct. - china_advantage: use only when research.china_advantage.supported is true. Put the concrete Chinese advantage or the foreign competitor's forced response in the foreground. The emotional direction must favor China.
- authority_breaks_consensus: the authority must be recognizable to a China audience, or be labeled by a meaningful role. Do not lead with an obscure romanized name.
- concrete_stakes: expose a specific number, forced choice, consequence, or who gains/loses. Generic importance is not a stake.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.

- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.

- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.

Tournament procedure, perform in this order:
1. Evidence veto: reject candidates that use a name, number, consensus, public action, comparison, or accusation not supported by that clip's transcript/research card.
2. China direction veto: for China-related clips, reject any candidate whose emotional target is China, Chinese people, Chinese companies, or China's future. Comparative pride is allowed only when supported.
3. Neutrality veto: reject flat summaries and generic questions. A question mark alone does not create tension.
4. Meta-copy veto: reject titles that expose the editor's reasoning with labels such as 外资策略师、外资首席、海外专家、西方策略师、罕见直言、外媒点破、终于有人说、只有外资敢说、大实话、 or 西方机构承认. The viewer should feel the effect from the facts, not be told how to feel.
5. Audience test: complete exactly one sentence: "看完标题，观众第一反应是____". If the answer is merely "我知道发生了什么", reject it.
6. Score survivors from 0-10. Final requires emotion_tension >= 8, novelty >= 7, specificity >= 7, curiosity_gap >= 7, factual_fidelity >= 9. For China clips, china_resonance >= 8.
7. Select the winner or combine only two candidates. If no candidate passes, write one new title, then score it honestly.
8. Before returning, verify every quality_check field. If any is false, rewrite once. Never return a known failure.

Editorial interpretation:
- 二极管 means one high-activation pole, not random anger: 意外, 惊喜, 强疑惑, 终于有人说, 有证据的言行反差, or 民族自豪.
- 新鲜感 requires a baseline plus a reversal. "外资谈中国" is ordinary; "外资在普遍悲观时罕见给出积极判断" is a usable reversal only if public_baseline supports it.
- 大实话 comes from who said what and why that identity makes the candor surprising. Do not paste "大实话" onto a routine forecast.
- 大实话、终于有人说、反差质疑 and 民族自豪 describe the intended viewer response internally. Do not print those labels or their editorial scaffolding in the title. Express them through the specific fact, comparison, and consequence.
- The desired effect of a possible falsehood angle is factual suspicion, not a verdict. Only when words_vs_actions is verified may you use a question such as "嘴上X，手里却Y？".
- "改口" means the same actor demonstrably held a different prior position. It requires research.position_change.supported and at least two independent sources. Never infer a change from search-result absence, lack of prior coverage, or a vague reputation.
- 民族自豪 comes from a concrete comparison: cost, technology, talent, supply chain, demand, speed, resilience, or a foreign competitor's forced adjustment. Do not use empty slogans.
- Familiar authority helps. Use a verified proper name only when the audience is likely to recognize it. Otherwise lead with the concrete subject; generic editorial identities such as 外资策略师、海外专家 or 西方策略师 are not final copy.
- Bloomberg/Bloomberg LP/彭博社 is normally the source, never the guest. Do not output 彭博有限合伙企业.
- Use only verified title_label values from this clip's entity/term card. Do not expand a familiar short name into a formal full name, and do not borrow an entity from another clip.

Title and display rules:
- Style: factual clickbait for China finance audience
- Use exactly three non-empty title lines, each a punchy cover block. Ideal lengths: 3-10, 4-12, 5-14 Chinese characters.
- Full title should be short and sharp, ideally 10-24 Chinese characters.
- Keep only one core conflict. Do not pack background, claim, caveat, and conclusion into one line.
- Highlights must be exact substrings of joined title_lines and emphasize the actor, number, reversal, China advantage, or tension.
- Do not use flat endings such as 回报路径在哪、回报存疑、前景如何、未来如何、有待观察、仍不明朗、面临挑战、带来机遇、释放信号、关键分叉在哪、有望扩大. Turn the caveat into a concrete unresolved action or contradiction.
- Every line must be a complete Chinese phrase. Do not leave a transitive tension verb such as 逼急、逼到、迫使 or 倒逼 without its subject or object.
- Do not use source badges, emojis, markdown, quotation marks, hashtags, or numbering.
- Title fields must not contain 资产管理、投资、股票、基金、理财、保险、投顾、荐股、买入、卖出.

- Do not mention sensitive geopolitical or military topics.

briefs.speaker: Kanhari Singh
briefs.speaker_context: Barclays, Head of Asia Equity Derivatives Sales (joining from Barclays Asia Forum in Singapore)
briefs.current_title: 巴克莱辛格：AI交易逻辑生变，亚洲科技谁主沉浮？

subtitles.zh: 当然，谢谢邀请我参加节目。
subtitles.en: Yeah, absolutely, I'm wanting even, and thanks for having me on.

subtitles.zh: 市场基本上在告诉我们，已经从交易AI氛围和叙事，转向对盈利超预期设定更高门槛。
subtitles.en: Look, I think markets are basically telling us that we are going on from, moving on from trading AI vibes and narrative, to now requiring a pretty high bar for what an earnings beat looks like.

subtitles.zh: 这既体现在资本开支的前瞻指引上，也体现在变现路径上。
subtitles.en: And you know, that's both in terms of capex forward guidance, but also for the path of monetization.

subtitles.zh: 隔夜看Meta和特斯拉，有两点很突出，
subtitles.en: And when I look at meta and Tesla overnight, the two things that stand out to me is,

subtitles.zh: 特斯拉的价格走势说得通，因为公司确实指引明年资本开支下降。
subtitles.en: you know, Tesla's price action kind of makes sense because the company did guide for lower capex next year.

subtitles.zh: 但Meta的数据客观上很强，然而亚洲今早开盘后，其股价却难以守住涨幅。
subtitles.en: But meta's numbers were objectively strong and yet the stock struggled to hold on to its gains when Asia came in this morning.

subtitles.zh: 这对亚洲后续走势的启示是，我们有三个科技表达指数，
subtitles.en: So what that tells me for the path ahead for Asia, where we have three indices, you know, for tech expression,

subtitles.zh: 韩国、台湾和日本，明年市场将更加挑剔。
subtitles.en: Korea, Taiwan and Japan, is that the market is going to be a lot more discerning next year.

subtitles.zh: 我认为要尊重价格走势，我们考虑做多优质资产。
subtitles.en: And I think respecting price action there, we think about being long quality.

subtitles.zh: 尤其是在科技领域，进入明年之际。
subtitles.en: Especially in the tech space, heading into next year.

briefs.current_title: 巴克莱辛格：中国政策信号转向，财政刺激为何不急？

subtitles.zh: 这是个好问题。思考中国大局，甚至回溯到重启交易，市场明显在寻找财政刺激的大标题。
subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, that's a pretty good question. I think when I think about the big picture in China, and even if I go as far back as the reopening trade, the market has clearly looked for some large headlines around fiscal stimulus.

subtitles.zh: 2024年9月我们确实看到了直接权益市场刺激。对我们来说，这在中国很多方面是一种实验，试图通过强力广泛支持权益市场，从消费者角度激发正向财富效应。
subtitles.en: And we did get that in terms of direct equity markets stimulus in September 2024. And you know, to us in many ways, that was China's way of kind of experimenting with trying to see if positive wealth effects can be kicked in on a consumer f

subtitles.zh: 但思考2025年，我们基本上已从中国权益市场中排除财政刺激的右尾风险。
subtitles.en: But when I think about 2025, we moved on to essentially price that right tail out from Chinese equity markets on fiscal stimulus.

subtitles.zh: 我认为有合理原因。看今年经济，中国增长呈非常K型路径，低于预期，但出口等领域受半导体驱动异常强劲。
subtitles.en: And I think for the right reasons, you know, when we look at the economy this year, it's been a very k-shaped path for China growth is below expectations, but pockets of the economy like exports are doing exceptionally strong driven by semi

subtitles.zh: 有趣的是，出口复苏在一定程度上与汇率强势脱钩，这说明中国在出口价值链上也在上移。
subtitles.en: What's been interesting is that that export recovery is somewhat decoupling from the effect strength as well, which tells you that China is moving up in the value chain of exports as well.

subtitles.zh: 所以从政策角度看，并不急于推出大规模财政刺激，权益市场支持仍非常有针对性以扭转局面。
subtitles.en: So I think from a policy perspective, there is no rush here to come in to do big fiscal stimulus and equity market support is still extremely targeted to turn things around.

briefs.speaker: Kanhari Singh
briefs.speaker_context: Barclays, Head of Asia Equity Derivatives Sales (joining from Barclays Asia Forum in Singapore)
briefs.current_title: 巴克莱辛格：印尼市场评级下调，被动资金流出压力几何？
current_title_lines: 被动资金流出压力几何？

subtitles.zh: 当然。我认为现在宣布确实令人意外，尽管之前明显有铺垫。
subtitles.en: Yeah, absolutely. Look, I think it's definitely been, you know, a surprise in terms of the announcement coming now, even though there was clearly a build up to it.

subtitles.zh: 印尼资产在这些水平相当便宜。权益资产显然有大波动，MSCI印尼前瞻估值现在是全球流动性变化以来最便宜。
subtitles.en: Indonesian assets are pretty cheap at these levels. Equities have obviously had some very large moves, MSCI Indonesia on a forward valuation basis is now as cheap as it's been since GFC.

subtitles.zh: 印尼盾实际汇率是20多年来最便宜。
subtitles.en: And the Indonesian rupee in real terms is the cheapest that it's been in over 20 years.

subtitles.zh: 所以显然印尼资产便宜，但我认为2027年6月前可能更便宜，除非治理方面有非常强的缓解因素。
subtitles.en: So clearly Indonesian assets are cheap, but I think there's a possibility that they get even cheaper in June, 20, 27 unless there are some very strong mitigating factors from a governance perspective.

subtitles.zh: 我们预计约150亿美元被动权益资金流出，认为美元印尼盾可能在明年二季度前升至1850水平。
subtitles.en: We're expecting about 15 billion US dollars in passive equity outflows and we think dollar idea is likely to grind higher to 18 to 50 level by a second quarter of next year.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这对权益资产意味着，除非MSCI希望看到的情况出现非常强的转变。
subtitles.en: And I think what that means for equities is, you know, unless again, there is a very strong turnaround in terms of what MSCI wants to see.

subtitles.zh: 权益资产反弹可能被卖出，进入明年。
subtitles.en: Equity rallies are probably going to be sold and you know, I'm heading into next year.

subtitles.zh: 我认为这仍是非常局部的国内故事，公告发布时印尼在新兴市场指数中权重为50个基点。
subtitles.en: I think this is a very localized domestic story still when this announcement came out Indonesia's weight in EM indices was 50 bips.

subtitles.zh: 所以这绝不是更广泛的新兴亚洲传染故事，尽管印尼本地波动剧烈。
subtitles.en: So by no means is this is this a broader even EM Asia contagion story, I would say as violent as the moves have been locally in Indonesia.

briefs.speaker: Marc Raibert
briefs.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute
briefs.current_title: 波士顿动力创始人：人形机器人竞赛，中国领先还是美国领先？
current_title_lines: 中国领先还是美国领先？

subtitles.zh: 您对这样的发展速度印象深刻吗？中国是否可能在人形机器人领域继续领先并扩大对美国的优势？
subtitles.en: Have you been impressed by the pace and could, you know, China continue to lead and extend its lead over the US perhaps when it comes to humanite robots.

subtitles.zh: 我不从竞争的角度思考，也不确定是否同意中国领先或不领先。但我确实认为现在是机器人领域的绝佳时机，关注度极高，资源丰富，投资者众多，大量事情正在发生。
subtitles.en: So, you know, I don't think in terms of a competition and I'm not sure I agree that China is leading or not leading. I do agree that it's a fantastic time to be in robotics. There's so much attention. There's so much resources, investors, a

subtitles.zh: 你说得对。过去几年，强化学习这项技术席卷全球。多个团队开创了这项工作，现在企业可以将这些技术应用到自己的机器人上。
subtitles.en: You're right. Over the last couple of years, reinforcement learning is a technique that's really swept the globe. A number of different groups originated the work and now it's made it possible for a company to take their robot, apply those

subtitles.zh: 几乎立刻就能让机器人做出令人兴奋的新动作，就像在中国奥运会上看到的那样，或其他公司运用这些技术所做的展示。
subtitles.en: And almost immediately get it to do new, exciting things like you see at the Chinese Olympics or you see other companies using those techniques to do.

subtitles.zh: 我们看到机器人举汽车、后空翻，但真正让机器人做人类动作一直很热门。我的同事大卫说，我们希望看到机器人拖地，但人类看似基本的动作并不容易做到。
subtitles.en: You know, we see those robots lifting cars and doing backflips, but it's been hot for robots to actually do human action. I mean, David, my colleague was talking about we would love to see a robot mopping the floor, but it's not that easy t

subtitles.zh: 完全正确。我认为部分问题在于人们不了解人类在自己所做的事情上有多出色。
subtitles.en: Absolutely true. I think part of the problem is that people don't understand how good human beings are at what they do.

subtitles.zh: 人类拥有多才多艺、灵巧以及其他特征。我认为根本问题在于，把这些机器人称为人形机器人本身就有问题。
subtitles.en: And what versatility and dexterity and other features that humans have. I mean, I think at the root of it, there's a problem even in calling these robots humanoid.

subtitles.zh: 因为人形意味着什么？是两条手臂、两条腿和一个头吗？为什么可能有上百家公司在制造有两条手臂、两条腿和一个头的机器人？
subtitles.en: Because what does humanoid mean? Does it mean two arms, two legs and a head? Why are there maybe a hundred companies building robots with two arms, two legs and a head?

subtitles.zh: 真正的人形应该意味着情境意识、理解周围环境、移动能力、灵巧性，以及用手或身体其他部位以有用方式移动物体的能力。
subtitles.en: When really humanoid should mean situational awareness, understanding our surroundings, mobility, dexterity, ability to use our hands or other parts of our body to move things around in a useful way.

subtitles.en: Semantic understanding, understanding the world in a deeper way. All those ingredients are what make humans good at what they do and some animals good at what they do.

briefs.current_title: 波士顿动力创始人：人形机器人五年后能做什么？仓库工厂先行，家庭尚远
current_title_lines: 仓库工厂先行，家庭尚远

subtitles.zh: 我认为如果我们专注于这一点，并涉及多种形态——形态意味着两条腿、两条手臂和一个头，或者轮子和另一种身体，或者六条手臂——那么像人类一样多才多艺和有用的可能性真的没有极限。
subtitles.en: And I think if we focused on that, with a variety of morphologies involved, morphologies means two legs, two arms and a head or wheels and some other kind of body or maybe six arms, there's really no limit to what could be versatile and use

subtitles.zh: 话虽如此，马克，我想知道哪些是炒作，哪些不是。五年后，这些你喜不喜欢这个称呼都罢的人形机器人，能做什么？
subtitles.en: So having said that, Mark, I'm wondering what's hype, what's not, five years down the road, what might these humanoid robots, whether you like the term or not, what would they be able to do?

subtitles.zh: 很难预测。容易说的是，各种形状和形式的机器人已经在仓库等场所使用，那些地方非常有序，物体处理量很大。
subtitles.en: It's hard to predict. I think that the easy thing to say is robots of various shapes and forms are already being used in warehouses and places like that, very organized things where there's objects being handled at very high volume.

subtitles.zh: 在难以获得人力劳动的地方，人力流动率高，人口老龄化，人口减少，年轻人对某些工作的态度在改变，一些群体的熟练劳动力正在老化退出。
subtitles.en: And where it's hard to get human labor, human labor has a lot of turnover, there's aging populations, reduced populations, a lot of the attitudes towards some kinds of work is changing among young people, some populations are aging out for

subtitles.zh: 所以机器人能做什么这个谜题有很多拼图。
subtitles.en: So there's a lot of pieces to the puzzle of what robots are going to be able to do.

subtitles.zh: 总之，我开始说，我认为仓库之后，工厂可能是下一个，家庭则要远一些，因为家庭需要大量安全保障，需要极致安全，需要低成本让消费者买得起，还需要它们能在家里做有用的事。
subtitles.en: Anyway, I start to say, I think warehouses are now factories are probably next, I think our homes are going to be a little ways out because for homes you need a lot of safety, you need really ultimate safety, you need low cost for consumers

subtitles.zh: 考虑到每个人的房子不同，杂物不同，孩子在场且脆弱，这确实是真正的挑战。
subtitles.en: And given that everybody's house is different, everybody's junk is different, everybody's kids are there and vulnerable, it's a real challenge.

briefs.speaker: Marc Raibert
briefs.speaker_context: Founder of Boston Dynamics and Executive Director of the Robotics and AI Institute
briefs.current_title: 波士顿动力创始人：机器人未来最兴奋的是什么？生产力机会巨大
current_title_lines: 最兴奋的是什么？生产力机会巨大

subtitles.zh: 让我们谈谈最积极的事情。
subtitles.en: So let's talk about the most positive thing.

subtitles.zh: 在机器人领域，你最兴奋的是什么？
subtitles.en: I mean, what are you most excited about when it comes to robotics?

subtitles.zh: 我们今天在哪里？
subtitles.en: Where are we today?

subtitles.zh: 我们将走向何方？
subtitles.en: Where are we headed?

subtitles.zh: 有没有可能发生难以想象的事情？
subtitles.en: I mean, anything that is possibly the unimaginable that could happen?

subtitles.zh: 我试着给出两种答案。
subtitles.en: I'll try and give two kinds of answers.

subtitles.zh: 我是研究员和开发者，对我来说不全是赚钱，而是取得技术进步和创造新事物。
subtitles.en: So I'm a researcher developer and it's not all about making money for me, it's about making the technical advances and creating new things.

subtitles.zh: 而且不一定看得到终点。
subtitles.en: And you know, there's no necessarily end point in sight.

subtitles.zh: 看看计算机。
subtitles.en: I mean, look at computers.

subtitles.zh: 他们造出又大又单一速度运行的计算机，然后它们变得更小更快。
subtitles.en: You know, they made computers that were big and operated at one speed and then they got smaller and faster.

subtitles.zh: 现在你可以随身携带，技术发展没有极限。
subtitles.en: Now that you can carry them around, there's no limit to where the technology goes.

subtitles.zh: 机器人也是如此。
subtitles.en: And robots are like that, too.

subtitles.zh: 现在很多人专注于制造有两条手臂、两条腿和一个头的东西，但也许我们会有些奇怪的新东西。
subtitles.en: You know, right now a lot of people are focused on trying to make things with two arms, two legs and a head, but you know, maybe we'll have some weird new thing that we're going to.

subtitles.zh: 这是我作为研究员的一面。
subtitles.en: So that's the researcher side of me.

subtitles.zh: 我确实认为每个人的生产力都有限制。
subtitles.en: I do think that there's limitations to productivity for everybody.

subtitles.zh: 正如我之前所说，人口老龄化，人口减少，人们不像以前那么愿意从事某些行业。
subtitles.en: I think the, as I said before, there's aging population, there's declining populations, there's people who don't really want to work in the trades as much as they did.

subtitles.zh: 别误会，机器人还做不到水管工或电工的工作，但我认为它们将来可以。
subtitles.en: Now don't get me wrong, robots aren't up to doing what a plumber or electrician does yet, but they will be, I think.

subtitles.zh: 所以有机会在不一定有足够人力做所有这些事的情况下实现高生产力。
subtitles.en: So there's an opportunity to have high productivity without necessarily having people available to do all those things.
